title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: RUTH ANN'S GAMBIT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Ruth Ann Dobbs, a retired hairdresser in Norfolk, Virginia.
She did hair for forty years. At seventy, she took on the toughest old man in the park.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE TABLES
segments.quote: The cure for boredom is curiosity. There is no cure for curiosity.
segments.author: Ellen Parr
lines: Retired life was too quiet. Ruth Ann had watched every cooking show twice.
One morning she passed the chess tables by the river. An old man said, ma'am, bingo is inside.
Then she remembered a line from her salon mirror, by the writer Ellen Parr:
The cure for boredom is curiosity. There is no cure for curiosity.
So Ruth Ann sat down and asked, which one is the horse?

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: FOUR MOVES
segments.quote: He who never made a mistake never made a discovery.
segments.author: Samuel Smiles
lines: He was Harold Pettiford, eighty-three, a retired tugboat captain. He beat her in four moves.
Harold wrote a line on a napkin, from the Scottish writer Samuel Smiles:
He who never made a mistake never made a discovery.
So Ruth Ann kept a notebook of every loss. By Labor Day, forty games. Forty lessons.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE HAIRCUT
segments.quote: While all artists are not chess players, all chess players are artists.
segments.author: Marcel Duchamp
lines: Harold's hair looked like a bird had moved in. So she offered a deal. One haircut for one lesson.
As she snipped, Harold quoted the French artist Marcel Duchamp:
While all artists are not chess players, all chess players are artists.
Well, she had been an artist for forty years. Now she studied the board like a fresh head of hair.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE NEW GUY
segments.quote: To teach is to learn twice.
segments.author: Joseph Joubert
lines: In October, a nervous young dockworker named Marcus sat down. Harold pointed at Ruth Ann. You teach him.
Me? I've lost forty games. Harold said, exactly. Then he quoted the French writer Joseph Joubert:
To teach is to learn twice.
So she showed Marcus every trap that ever caught her. And explaining them, she finally understood them.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: DOWN A QUEEN
segments.quote: We learn by chess the habit of not being discouraged by present bad appearances in the state of our affairs.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: That fall, the park held a tournament. In the semifinal, a cocky young man took her queen and started packing his bag.
Then she remembered Benjamin Franklin, who loved this game:
We learn by chess the habit of not being discouraged by present bad appearances in the state of our affairs.
So she kept going, one quiet move at a time. Forty moves later, he was the surprised one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FINAL
segments.quote: In war, resolution; in defeat, defiance; in victory, magnanimity; in peace, goodwill.
segments.author: Winston Churchill
lines: In the final, she faced Harold. And she won.
She wanted to dance on the table. But she remembered Winston Churchill:
In war, resolution; in defeat, defiance; in victory, magnanimity; in peace, goodwill.
Magnanimity means being big about it. So she shook Harold's hand and bought coffee for the whole park.
Then she taped up a new sign. Bingo is inside. Everybody is welcome out here.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Stay curious. Collect mistakes. Make it art. Teach someone. Don't quit. Win kindly.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Stay curious. Collect your mistakes. Make it art. Teach someone. Don't quit when you're behind. Win kindly.
I play chess too. My cat usually wins.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
